about: Every new check proposed by the evidence connectors research, deduplicated. Proposal only: nothing here is in seed content. Shape follows seed/content/automation/checks.json plus the fields listed in fields.

fields.capability_match: absent means all listed capabilities must be connected, as in checks.json today. each means every connected provider of a listed capability is evaluated on its own and the check passes only when all of them pass; requires lists capabilities that must also be connected for the comparison. Needs an engine change (see 05-check-registry.md).
fields.observation_types: from 01-evidence-model.md 1.4, plus new types listed in observation_types_added
fields.providers: provider key to supported, partial or not_possible, from the feasibility tables
fields.artifacts: artifact keys from artifacts.json, or from artifacts_proposed below
fields.aliases: keys other researchers used for the same predicate; they are not to be created
fields.related: keys with a similar aim that stay separate, with the reason
fields.artifacts_from_needs: artifacts that reach the check through a NEED resolved in coverage/needs-resolution.json

checks.name: Identity provider access reviews are finished
checks.description: Every access review that closed in the period has a decision on every item by someone other than the person reviewed, and every removal decided was applied.
checks.remediation: Finish open reviews, reassign self reviews, and apply the removals that were decided.

controls.rationale: Shows reviews run inside the identity provider were completed and acted on. Systems outside it and the review procedure stay with people.
Where privileged roles are reviewed in the identity provider, shows those reviews were completed.

provider_notes.entra: Needs Entra ID Governance, or P2 for features GA in P2, and the optional AccessReview.Read.All permission; without them error with reason licence. Decision field names unverified.
provider_notes.okta: Needs Okta Identity Governance and the optional okta.governance.accessCertifications.read scope; not applicable without it.
provider_notes.gws: Workspace has no access review feature.

checks.population: Review instances that ended in the last 90 days
checks.predicate: No item without a decision; no item decided by the person it is about; every deny decision applied
checks.period: 90 days ending at collection
checks.empty_population: `not_applicable` when the customer runs reviews outside the identity provider (the manual review pack stays the evidence), never `pass`
checks.notes: New observation type proposed: identity.access_review (review instance, decisions, reviewer, principal, apply result); none of the 1.4 types fits. Fills completed-access-reviews-with-reviewer-sign only where the customer reviews inside Entra or Okta.

checks.name: Administrators use phishing resistant sign in
checks.description: Every account that holds an administrator role must sign in with a phishing resistant factor, such as a security key or a passkey.
checks.remediation: Require a phishing resistant factor for administrator roles, and enrol a security key or passkey for each listed administrator.

controls.rationale: Shows identity provider administrators must use a phishing resistant factor. Cloud root accounts and other systems are checked separately.
Shows privileged identity provider accounts carry stronger sign in protection. Approval and review of those accounts stay with people.

provider_notes.entra: Needs P1: an enabled Conditional Access policy targeting the admin roles with an authentication strength of phishing resistant methods only (FIDO2, Windows Hello for Business, certificate based multifactor). Security defaults alone fail; no P1 fails with reason plan. Method value names to confirm.
provider_notes.okta: Whether Okta Verify counts as phishing resistant depends on its configuration (unverified), so those admins read insufficient. The Admin Console policy constraint field name is unverified. Role read may need more than Read-only Administrator.
provider_notes.gws: Uses security key and passkey counts from usage reports, which are 1 to 5 days late, and the 2SV factor policy (PASSKEY_ONLY or a passkey combination). How a policy targets a group is unverified. The policy part errors without a super admin subject.

checks.population: Enabled accounts holding any administrator role (active or eligible) at collection time
checks.predicate: A policy that applies to the account requires a phishing resistant factor, and the account has one enrolled
checks.period: Point in time, daily
checks.empty_population: `error`: an identity provider always has at least one administrator, so an empty list means the role read failed
checks.notes: Fills second-factor-enforcement-and-enrolled-users for IAM-03.C (idp.mfa_enforced fills B, D, E). 1Password is n/a in the matrix. implementations in identity-checks.md say empty until a collector ships; here they follow the brief (supported or partial providers).

checks.name: App credentials have owners and expire
checks.description: Every application or service app that holds a credential in the identity provider has a named owner, and no credential lives longer than the rotation limit.
checks.remediation: Add an owner to the listed applications, and replace credentials that outlive the rotation limit.

controls.rationale: Covers machine identities held in the identity provider. Cloud and build system credentials are checked by `cloud.machine_credentials_rotated`.

provider_notes.entra: App registrations with a secret or certificate: owners and credential start and end dates (never secret values).
provider_notes.okta: Okta apps have no owner field (unverified), so only credential age is judged; API tokens are judged as tied to an active admin. The token listing endpoint and scope are unverified.
provider_notes.gws: Service accounts and delegation clients live in Google Cloud, not the Workspace directory (no Admin SDK listing found, unverified). Covered by cloud.machine_credentials_rotated.

parameters.max_credential_days: default 365, from the customer's access policy

checks.population: Applications registered in the customer's own directory that hold at least one secret or certificate
checks.predicate: At least one owner, and every credential's lifetime (end minus start, or age where no end exists) is at most `max_credential_days`
checks.period: Point in time, daily
checks.empty_population: `pass` with a note when the list was complete (many small tenants have none)
checks.notes: identity.app in 01-evidence-model 1.4 has no owner or credential date fields; extend it with owners and credential dates, or add a new observation type identity.app_credential. records-of-rotation-or-review is filled for IAM-10.D.

checks.name: No unused account stays active
checks.description: No enabled account, member or guest, has gone longer than the allowed period without a successful sign in.
checks.remediation: Disable the listed accounts, or record why each one must stay active.

controls.rationale: Finds accounts nobody uses, which is how missed removals surface. Matching accounts to leavers needs the staff list.
Points reviewers at unused access between reviews. The review and its sign off stay with people.
Finds guest and contractor accounts that outlived their use. The contractor register and end dates stay with people.

evidence_kinds: Account list with last successful sign in

provider_notes.entra: Supported with P1 only: signInActivity needs P1 or P2, so a Free tenant reads error with reason licence. lastSuccessfulSignInDateTime exists only from December 2023; before that use the later of the interactive and non interactive times. A guest still PendingAcceptance counts as inactive. signInActivity reads are limited to 10 a minute.
provider_notes.okta: lastLogin; null means never signed in. Deprovisioned users must be queried explicitly.
provider_notes.gws: The later of lastLoginTime and accounts:timestamp_last_sso.
provider_notes.onepassword: The Users API has no last sign in field.

related.why: User accounts against cloud passwords and access keys.

parameters.inactive_days: default 90, set from the customer's access policy; accounts created less recently than this are left out

checks.population: Enabled accounts older than `inactive_days`, members and guests, excluding accounts recorded as exceptions in Verity
checks.predicate: Last successful sign in is within `inactive_days`. An account that never signed in counts as inactive
checks.period: Rolling window of `inactive_days` ending at collection
checks.empty_population: `pass` only when the provider returned a complete user list; otherwise `insufficient information`
checks.notes: Fills account-list-export for IAM-12.E. Related, not an alias: people.accounts_match_roster (members against the roster; guests are covered here).

checks.name: Leavers lose password manager access
checks.description: No one who left still has an active company password manager account after the allowed time.
checks.remediation: Suspend the listed password manager accounts, and rotate the shared credentials they could read.

controls.rationale: Shows leavers lost vault access. Rotating the shared credentials they could read is recorded by people.
Covers the password manager, one of the systems outside single sign on that removal must reach.

provider_notes.onepassword: Needs a leaver roster. Removal time from the suspend or delete audit event (Events Reporting token, auditevents only), else the first daily snapshot showing the member gone or suspended. The Users API is not available on Teams or when the account uses 1Password automated provisioning; then membership comes from the identity provider's assignment of the 1Password app and the evidence says so.

related.why: Same leaver population and removal time, on the password manager instead of the identity provider.

checks.population: Leavers on the roster whose end date is in the last 90 days
checks.predicate: No active vault account for the leaver later than `removal_hours` after the end date
checks.period: 90 days ending at collection
checks.empty_population: `pass` only when the roster is current and shows no leavers; otherwise `insufficient information`
checks.notes: New observation type proposed: vault.event (password manager audit events: suspend, delete, vault access grant and revoke). Fills removal-records-for-a-sample-of for IAM-12.D and password-manager-members-against-staff-list for IAM-05.B and D (IAM-05.C stays a person). Same predicate shape as people.leavers_deprovisioned on a different system and shares removal_hours; kept separate because multiple capabilities on a check mean all are needed. 1Password marks people.leavers_deprovisioned n/a and points here. Related NEED password_manager: every shared vault has a named owner and members that match its team (IAM-05.C); no read only, complete API lists vault access, so no check is proposed.

checks.name: Every account belongs to a current person
checks.description: Every enabled member account in the identity provider matches a person on the current staff and contractor roster, or is a recorded shared or service account with an owner.
checks.remediation: Disable the listed accounts, link each to a person, or record it as a service account with an owner.

controls.rationale: Reconciles accounts with the people who should have them. Systems outside the identity provider need their own reconciliation.
Shows each account maps to one named person. Approval of the access is checked separately.
Shows contractor accounts match the contractor roster. Agreements and training stay with people.

provider_notes.entra: Needs a roster. Match by employee id or UPN.
provider_notes.okta: Needs a roster. Population is users that can sign in.
provider_notes.gws: Needs a roster. Shared or service mailboxes can be recorded as such.

checks.population: Enabled member accounts (guests are covered by `idp.no_inactive_accounts`)
checks.predicate: Matched to an active roster person by immutable id, or by email when the roster has no id, or recorded in Verity as a shared or service account with an owner
checks.period: Point in time, daily
checks.empty_population: `insufficient information` when no roster exists or it is older than its own review period
checks.notes: Fills account-list-export for IAM-12.E and HR-03.B. contractor-register-with-start-and-end is an input, unchanged. hr_system providers are not_planned in capabilities.json; until a roster exists in Verity (continuous compliance plan 6 C proposes a controlled workforce import) it reads insufficient information. Related: idp.no_inactive_accounts, edge.members_current.

checks.name: Screening finished before start
checks.description: Every worker who started in the last 12 months has a completed, cleared screening record dated on or before the start date.
checks.remediation: Record the screening result for each listed joiner, or record why screening finished after the start date.

controls.rationale: Shows a cleared check is recorded before each start. The scope by role, legal limits per country and rechecks stay with people.

evidence_kinds: Per joiner: start date, screening type, completion date, cleared yes or no

provider_notes.bamboohr: Only with a mapped custom field; no screening module found (unverified).
provider_notes.rippling: Not found in the public API index (unverified).
provider_notes.workday: Only if the customer uses the Workday recruiting background check step and adds it to the report (unverified).

parameters.screening field: tenant setting naming the HR field that holds the screening result

checks.population: Workers whose start date is in the last 12 months; optionally moves into roles the tenant marks as sensitive.
checks.predicate: A screening record or a mapped HR field shows a completed, cleared check dated on or before the start date (or the move date).
checks.period: Start dates in the last 12 months, evaluated daily.
checks.empty_population: Not stated; insufficient under the shared rules.
checks.notes: Outcomes: fail when missing, not cleared, or dated after the start; insufficient when no screening source or field is mapped, or the field is restricted. HiBob screening support is unverified and not classified. D-HR-4 proposes a background_screening capability in a later round; until then HR fields only. Verity keeps only date, type and cleared yes or no, never the report content. Uses the NEW observation type person.screening (hr-systems.md section 3).

checks.name: Contractors have an end date
checks.description: Every active contractor has a recorded end date that is today or later.
checks.remediation: Record the contract end date for each listed contractor, or end the record if the contract has finished.

controls.rationale: Shows each contractor has a fixed end date. Sponsor, access scope, agreements and return of equipment stay with people.

evidence_kinds: Contractor list with start and end dates

provider_notes.bamboohr: Contractor type from the employment status field; the contract end date field is often custom and the tenant maps it.
provider_notes.workday: Yes if the contract end date is in the customer built report (unverified).
provider_notes.gusto: Contractor end dates unverified; the contractors endpoint is separate and its path and fields are unverified.
provider_notes.hibob: Yes if contract end is a field the tenant maps.

parameters.contractor employment types: tenant setting mapping provider values to contractor

checks.population: Active workers whose employment type is contractor (provider mapping, extendable by the tenant).
checks.predicate: An end date is recorded and is today or later.
checks.period: Daily snapshot.
checks.empty_population: Not stated in hr-systems.md; under the shared rules insufficient, unless a complete HR read shows there are no contractor records.
checks.notes: Outcomes: fail when there is no end date, or the end date has passed while the record is still active; insufficient when the employment type is not readable. Fills contractor-register-with-start-and-end partially (access and sponsor are not in HR). The roster import CSV carries type and end, but no document lists roster_import for this check.

checks.name: People list exports from the HR system
checks.description: The HR system's full worker list was read, and every active worker and recent leaver has the fields onboarding and offboarding are measured against.
checks.remediation: Fill the missing fields (work email, start date, employment type, manager, end date) in the HR system for the listed workers, or give Verity's credential access to former workers and restricted fields.

controls.rationale: Gives the leaver list and end dates offboarding is measured against; the offboarding itself is checked elsewhere.
Gives the joiner list onboarding is tested against.
The leaver list matches the HR tool (IAM-12.B); removal is checked by people.leavers_deprovisioned.
The complete list of joiners the screening sample is drawn from.
The staff roster side of the device reconciliation in EP-03.C (strategy section 3).
With hr.contractors_have_end_dates, evidences that the contractor register is complete (HR-03.B, strategy section 3).

evidence_kinds: Dated roster: worker id, name, work email, employment type, start, end, termination type where present, manager id, department, title, status
Joiners, leavers and movers since the last run

provider_notes.bamboohr: GET /api/v1/employees with fields=, both statuses read; watch _restrictedFields; never filter on a restricted field; never use employees/directory (it omits former employees). Employment type field name unverified.
provider_notes.rippling: GET /workers/ with workers.read; query each status explicitly because the default list may omit TERMINATED. The token is revoked if its owner is terminated or it is unused for 30 days.
provider_notes.workday: By report design: a customer built Report as a Service run by an Integration System User, including contingent workers and terminated workers within 13 months. Everything about Workday is unverified.
provider_notes.gusto: Employees and contractors read separately; the contractors endpoint is unverified. Verity must pass Gusto's partner review before any customer can connect.
provider_notes.hibob: Only if showInactive is set and the service user's access rights include former employees (the default covers active only). HiBob silently omits fields the service user cannot see.
provider_notes.roster_import: CSV roster (worker id, email, type, start, end, manager). Read as insufficient for completeness, because a file cannot prove it is the whole list; its rows are a person's evidence and the roster artifact keeps its person source.

checks.population: All worker records: active, plus anyone whose end date is in the last 13 months. Pre start records (offer accepted, not started) are listed but not counted.
checks.predicate: The read was complete; every active worker has a work email, start date, employment type and manager (people marked as top of the organisation excepted); every worker who left in the window has an end date.
checks.period: Daily, with leavers kept 13 months after their end date so a 12 month Type 2 window is always covered.
checks.empty_population: Insufficient.
checks.notes: Outcomes: pass when complete and every record has the fields; fail when records miss a field, each listed; error on a credential or permission problem; insufficient when paging was cut short, fields are restricted, or inactive workers are not readable. Fills roster-of-joiners-and-leavers-with FULL (F3 and hr-systems.md section 10: it is the roster itself), replacing people.leavers_deprovisioned on that artifact; the artifact is named by 17 objectives (CS-04.C, EP-03.C, EP-05.C, GOV-04.B, GOV-09.C, GOV-21.D, HR-01.B, HR-02.B, HR-05.C, HR-05.D, HR-06.B, HR-08.C, IAM-05.B, IAM-12.B, IAM-12.E, NS-11.C, PE-02.B). A pass says the HR list is well formed, not that every worker is in it (contractors paid through accounts payable often never appear); the identity research's NEW people.accounts_match_roster (identity-checks.md 2.5) covers the gap and uses this HR side. The EP-03 and HR-03 mappings come from strategy section 3 objective tables; hr-systems.md 2.2 maps only HR-05, HR-06, IAM-12 and HR-01. Back dated terminations: keep the first time Verity saw the termination and report both. Key on worker id (rehires reuse emails). Data minimisation per D-HR-3. Uses the NEW observation type person.event (hr-systems.md section 3).

checks.name: Security training is current
checks.description: Every active worker completed security awareness training within the refresher interval, and each joiner within the set days of starting.
checks.remediation: Assign security awareness training to the listed people and follow up until it is completed.

controls.rationale: Shows completion against the staff list. Content, role modules and chasing overdue people stay with people.

evidence_kinds: Per person: training type, completion date

provider_notes.bamboohr: Yes if the company uses BambooHR training: GET /api/v1/training/record/employee/{employeeId}, one call per employee; OAuth scope training.
provider_notes.rippling: Not found in the public API index (unverified).

related.why: Training in the HR system against in house material acknowledged in Verity.

parameters.contractors with access: setting, whether they are in the population

checks.population: Active workers on the run date; contractors with access per setting.
checks.predicate: A completed training of a type the tenant marks as security awareness within refresher_interval_months, and for joiners within training_due_days of the start date.
checks.period: Daily snapshot.
checks.empty_population: Not stated; insufficient under the shared rules.
checks.notes: Outcomes: fail when missing or older than the interval; insufficient when no training source is mapped. HiBob training support is unverified and not classified. D-HR-4 proposes a security_training capability in a later round (it may overlap with a learning platform capability proposed by other research). hr-systems.md section 10 says it fills completion-records-for-all-staff for HR-08.B, HR-08.C, HR-06.E and HR-03.C; that artifact is also named by DM-04.D (classification training) and HR-07.D (skills gaps), so the fill must stay partial or a security awareness check would satisfy them. Uses the NEW observation type person.training (hr-systems.md section 3).

checks.name: Every company device belongs to a current person
checks.description: Every company owned managed device is assigned to an active member account in the identity provider.
checks.remediation: Assign each listed device to its current user, or recover it from the person who left and reassign or retire it.

controls.rationale: Reconciles devices to the staff list from the device side.
Each device has an accountable person.

evidence_kinds: Per device: assigned email, account state

provider_notes.intune: userId or userPrincipalName joined to the Entra user's accountEnabled (Entra ID connector, User.Read.All already held). Shared and kiosk devices need an exclusion with a reason.
provider_notes.jamf: Needs an identity provider. userAndLocation.email joined to the IdP. Jamf's user field is often free text: match on email only, never on display name.
provider_notes.kandji: Needs an identity provider. Device user (or GET /api/v1/users email) joined to the IdP.
provider_notes.gws: deviceUsers.userEmail joined to the Workspace user's state (identity connector).

checks.population: Company owned managed devices; shared or kiosk devices excluded with a reason.
checks.predicate: The assigned user matches an active member account in the identity provider.
checks.period: Daily snapshot.
checks.empty_population: Insufficient (shared rule 5.1).
checks.notes: Outcomes: fail when unassigned, or assigned to a suspended, deleted or unknown account; insufficient when the identity list is incomplete. Serves EP-03.C and, in spirit, LM-01.B: until the device asset type is decided (D-DEV-6) this gives each device an accountable person and the device inventory artifact stays separate from the asset inventory (strategy section 3, LM-01). People match on lowercased work email, then the IdP's immutable user id. Needs the new device fields 'assigned user email and provider user id' (mdm doc section 6).

checks.name: Laptop firewalls are on
checks.description: Every managed macOS, Windows and Linux computer has its native firewall turned on.
checks.remediation: Turn on the native firewall through an MDM policy or profile on the listed computers, on Windows for every profile.

controls.rationale: Shows the firewall part of the baseline holds. Other baseline settings and the policy are separate.

evidence_kinds: Per device firewall state and source

provider_notes.intune: Windows from the Intune FirewallStatus report (beta export job; path and the permission it needs are unverified). macOS from a compliance policy firewall setting and the device status (property name unverified).
provider_notes.jamf: security.firewallEnabled from the v4 computers inventory.
provider_notes.gws: 5.5 says 'likely'. Endpoint Verification additionalSignals firewall status; value format unverified. A reported signal, not enforced.

parameters.stale_after_days: 14. A device not checked in within this many days gives insufficient for that device

checks.population: Managed macOS, Windows and Linux computers in scope.
checks.predicate: The native firewall is on (Windows: every profile, or the provider's firewall health is good).
checks.period: Daily snapshot.
checks.empty_population: Insufficient (shared rule 5.1).
checks.notes: Outcomes: fail when off; insufficient when not reported. Serves EP-03.D (baseline applied). No artifact is named for it: EP-03.D tests inventory-of-company-devices, patch-compliance-report and screen-lock-setting-report, and the F1 split does not say which artifact carries baseline settings such as the firewall. Strategy section 3 ('Malware and patching across families') also says device checks cover part of the OS hardening in NS-04 (firewall), but no NS-04 mapping is proposed in the check table. The device field 'firewall on' is already in 01-evidence-model 1.4 and restated in mdm doc section 6.

checks.name: Leavers' devices come back or are wiped
checks.description: Every device assigned to a person who left was wiped with confirmation, returned, or reassigned within the allowed days after the end date.
checks.remediation: Recover or wipe the listed devices and record the outcome, or reassign them to an active person.

controls.rationale: Shows unreturned devices were wiped.
Covers the device return item of offboarding.
Covers device return at a contractor's end date.

evidence_kinds: Per leaver: end date, devices, outcome and its date

provider_notes.intune: Devices assigned to a leaver at the end date, then a wipe or retire in deviceActionResults with a completed state, or the device record retired, or reassigned. Retired devices leave the list, so only Verity's daily snapshots keep the history. Needs an HR source.
provider_notes.jamf: Leaver's devices, then an erase command with dateCompleted, an unmanage, or a reassignment. Needs Verity's own daily history and an HR source.
provider_notes.kandji: Erase command completed (date_completed), removal, or reassignment after the end date. Command status integers are undocumented, so only a set date_completed counts as done.
provider_notes.gws: Device or device user managementState WIPED after the leaver's end date. An account wipe on a personal phone counts only if the policy says so.

parameters.leaver_device_days: 7. Days after the end date by which the device must be wiped, returned or reassigned
parameters.lookback_days: 90. Window of end dates looked at

checks.population: Devices assigned, on Verity's own record, to a person whose end date is within lookback_days and at least leaver_device_days ago (contractors at their end date count).
checks.predicate: Within leaver_device_days of the end date the device was wiped with confirmation, unenrolled with a recorded return, or reassigned to an active person.
checks.period: End dates in the last lookback_days, evaluated daily.
checks.empty_population: Not stated in the doc; insufficient under shared rule 5.1 unless the HR read proves there were no leavers with devices.
checks.notes: Outcomes: fail when still assigned to the leaver, or no recorded outcome; insufficient when Verity has no observation of the device at the end date (connected later) or the HR list is incomplete. Needs an HR source or the roster import (roster_import). Serves EP-05.C, HR-05.E and HR-03.D (strategy section 3). Only wipe-confirmations-for-recovered-or-lost is named as its artifact (intune.md section 6). HR-05.E and HR-03.D test completed-offboarding-records-for-leavers-in, contractor-register-with-start-and-end and removal-records-for-a-sample-of; no document proposes adding this check to those. Uses the NEW observation type device.action (mdm doc section 6: device, kind wipe, lock or retire, issued at, completed at, state, source).

checks.name: Disk recovery keys are held centrally
checks.description: Every encrypted device has its OS volume recovery key held by the MDM or the directory, without Verity ever reading the key.
checks.remediation: Escrow the FileVault or BitLocker recovery key to the MDM or the directory for the listed devices, for example by rotating the key under an escrow policy or profile.

controls.rationale: Shows encrypted devices stay recoverable. Encryption itself, exceptions and the policy are separate.

evidence_kinds: Per device: escrow present, source, key created date

provider_notes.intune: Windows only (5.5 says 'Windows'): a BitLocker key record whose deviceId equals the device's azureADDeviceId, read with BitlockerKey.ReadBasic.All (metadata only, never the key). FileVault escrow is not exposed in Graph v1.0 as far as read (unverified), so macOS gives insufficient.
provider_notes.jamf: individualRecoveryKeyValidityStatus valid, or institutionalRecoveryKeyPresent, from the v4 computers inventory DISK_ENCRYPTION section. Value names unverified.
provider_notes.kandji: 5.5 says 'likely'. Device details FileVault escrow field (a third party sample shows filevault_prk_escrowed, unverified) or Prism filevault. Confirm the field.
provider_notes.gws: Not reported by Google: insufficient.

parameters.stale_after_days: 14. A device not checked in within this many days gives insufficient for that device

checks.population: Devices passing the devices.disk_encrypted predicate.
checks.predicate: A recovery key for the OS volume is held by the MDM or the directory. Key material is never read.
checks.period: Daily snapshot. The daily history shows the key was held throughout the period.
checks.empty_population: Insufficient (shared rule in mdm doc 5.1: an empty population is insufficient unless the check can prove emptiness).
checks.notes: Outcomes: fail when no key is held; insufficient when the provider does not report escrow for that platform. Serves EP-02.B (every device encrypted, key held centrally). Needs the new device observation field 'recovery key escrowed' (mdm doc section 6). Never request permissions that expose keys: Intune BitlockerKey.Read.All, Jamf 'View Disk Encryption Recovery Key', Kandji /secrets/filevaultkey.

checks.name: USB storage is blocked or restricted
checks.description: Every managed company Windows and macOS device has an applied policy that blocks removable storage or allows only encrypted media.
checks.remediation: Assign a restrictions profile or device control policy that blocks removable storage, or allows only encrypted media, to the listed devices.

controls.rationale: Covers the removable media route only. Other routes, alerts and reviews stay with people.

provider_notes.intune: 5.5 says 'later'. Needs the per device status of a configuration or endpoint security policy that blocks removable storage. Per device configuration state is not on the v1.0 device resource and the reports route is unverified. Recorded as not_possible for the first version.
provider_notes.jamf: A restrictions profile blocking external media installed on the device (Read macOS Configuration Profiles). Payload keys to confirm.
provider_notes.kandji: Library item status for a restrictions profile.
provider_notes.gws: Not reported.

checks.population: Managed Windows and macOS company devices in scope.
checks.predicate: A policy or profile that blocks removable storage, or allows only encrypted media, is assigned and reported applied.
checks.period: Daily snapshot.
checks.empty_population: Insufficient (shared rule 5.1).
checks.notes: Outcomes: fail when none is applied; insufficient when the provider cannot report it. Serves DM-19.C (ISO A.5.14, A.7.10, A.8.12 full). leakage-prevention-and-sharing-settings-in is also named by DM-19.A and DM-19.B (email, chat and file tool settings), so this check can only fill it partially. Needs the new device field 'removable storage blocked' (mdm doc section 6).

checks.name: Every person works on a managed device
checks.description: Every active member account has at least one managed device assigned to it that is in contact.
checks.remediation: Enrol a company device for each listed person, or record why they have none (for example no company device by role).

controls.rationale: Reconciles the staff list to managed devices, which is how unmanaged laptops are found.

evidence_kinds: Per person: devices and their state

provider_notes.intune: Entra member users, minus exclusions, each with one managed device in contact. Guests and service accounts are taken from the Entra observation 'kind'.
provider_notes.jamf: Needs an identity provider. Person direction of the email join.
provider_notes.kandji: Needs an identity provider. Person direction of the same join.
provider_notes.gws: 5.5 says partial; google-endpoint-management.md 5.2 says 'yes' but depends on the devices.enrolled decision (D-DEV-9). If Endpoint Verification desktops count only as known, a person with only such a desktop fails.

parameters.stale_after_days: 14. A device out of contact longer than this does not count

checks.population: Active member accounts (not guests or service accounts), minus people excluded with a reason (for example no company device by role).
checks.predicate: At least one managed device is assigned and in contact.
checks.period: Daily snapshot.
checks.empty_population: Insufficient (shared rule 5.1).
checks.notes: Outcomes: fail when the person has no device, or only out of contact devices; insufficient when the device or identity read is incomplete. Gives the completeness that devices.enrolled cannot (an MDM cannot see devices that never enrolled) for EP-03.B, and the reconciliation for EP-03.C. Conflict on the Google level: strategy 5.5 partial versus connector file yes; partial kept.

checks.name: Wipes are confirmed, not assumed
checks.description: Every wipe command issued in the window reached a completed state, or the device later reported itself wiped.
checks.remediation: Follow up each failed, cancelled or long pending wipe: issue it again, or record the device as lost and rotate the credentials it held.

controls.rationale: Shows each wipe executed. Why it was issued and credential rotation stay with people.

evidence_kinds: Per command: device, issued, completed, state

provider_notes.intune: deviceActionResults wipe entries with their state and times. actionState values and how long results stay on the record are unverified. Intune audit events would be the stronger source; their permission was not verified.
provider_notes.jamf: Erase commands sent in the window with status and dateCompleted (GET /api/v2/mdm/commands, a filter is required). Command enum names, retention and the Jamf Pro privilege name are unverified.
provider_notes.kandji: Erase commands in the window with date_completed. Status integers are undocumented: require date_completed.
provider_notes.gws: WIPING then WIPED transitions in Verity's daily history; the admin audit log as the event source (application and event names unverified).

parameters.wipe pending limit: 7 days. The doc calls it a setting but gives it no name

checks.population: Every wipe command issued in lookback_days.
checks.predicate: The command reached a completed state, or the device later reported wiped.
checks.period: Commands issued in the last lookback_days, evaluated daily.
checks.empty_population: Not stated in the doc; insufficient under shared rule 5.1 unless the provider can prove no wipe was issued in the window.
checks.notes: Outcomes: fail when failed, cancelled, or pending past 7 days; insufficient when the command history is not readable or is shorter than the window. Serves EP-05.D. Uses the NEW observation type device.action (mdm doc section 6).

checks.name: Every managed laptop runs the protection agent
checks.description: Every managed company computer in contact has a matching protection sensor that meets the endpoint.protection_active freshness rule.
checks.remediation: Install or reconnect the protection agent on the listed computers.

controls.rationale: Shows the agent reaches every managed laptop, checked against the device inventory.

evidence_kinds: Per device: match key, sensor id, last seen

provider_notes.defender_endpoint: Needs an MDM. Every MDM device in contact matches a machine by aadDeviceId (Intune), or by hostname then MAC for other MDMs (serial is not on the machine resource as read, so weaker). Non Entra joined devices match on name only and the results say so.
provider_notes.crowdstrike: Needs an MDM. MDM devices matched to hosts by serial_number, then hostname and MAC.
provider_notes.sentinelone: Needs an MDM. Match on serial number if the agent reports it (unverified), then computer name. All SentinelOne fields unverified.

parameters.stale_after_days: 14. Devices out of contact longer are not in the population

checks.population: Managed company computers in contact, from the device_management provider.
checks.predicate: A matching sensor passes the endpoint.protection_active freshness rule.
checks.period: Daily snapshot.
checks.empty_population: Insufficient (shared rule 5.1).
checks.notes: Outcomes: fail when there is no matching sensor, or a stale one; insufficient when either read is incomplete. The device side can come from any device_management provider (intune, jamf, kandji, gws); Google Endpoint Verification can feed it only as the device population. A match made on name alone is labelled weak. The connector files name the artifact as 'inventory-of-company-devices (protection coverage part)', which after the F1 split is the proposed device-protection-agent-report. Uses the NEW observation type endpoint.sensor (mdm doc section 6: or protection fields on device).

checks.name: Endpoint alerts are handled in time
checks.description: Endpoint alerts at or above the minimum severity are triaged and closed within the set times, and every closed alert has an owner and a classification.
checks.remediation: Assign, triage and close the listed alerts, recording the owner and the classification or resolution.

controls.rationale: Shows alerts were reviewed and closed. Whether one became an incident stays with people.
Shows endpoint events were assessed.

evidence_kinds: Per alert: severity, status, owner, created, closed, classification

provider_notes.defender_endpoint: Alerts in the window with status, assignedTo, classification and resolvedTime (GET /api/alerts, or Graph /v1.0/security/alerts_v2). No status history: time to triage cannot be measured, only that nothing stays New past the limit. Alert.Read.All is not listed on the List alerts page (only Alert.ReadWrite.All): test read only access, else use Graph SecurityAlert.Read.All, never accept a write permission. Retention 180 days by default (unverified). Alert data on Plan 1 unverified.
provider_notes.crowdstrike: Alerts v2 in the window: none still new after the triage limit, none open past the close limit, closed ones with an assignee. Status values in_progress and reopened confirmed; new and closed unverified. No status history.
provider_notes.sentinelone: Threats in the window by incident status and analyst verdict (values unverified). No status history.

checks.population: Alerts at or above alert_min_severity created in lookback_days.
checks.predicate: None is still new after alert_triage_hours; none is open past alert_close_days for its severity; every closed alert has an owner and a classification or resolution.
checks.period: Alerts created in the last lookback_days, evaluated daily.
checks.empty_population: Pass with the reason 'no alerts in the window', only when the query covered the whole window.
checks.notes: Outcomes: fail on any breach, each listed; insufficient when the alert query is incomplete or provider retention is shorter than the window. Fills alerts-that-were-reviewed-and-acted partially: EP-01.C, and EP-01.D also needs the incident register (NEED ticketing: high and critical true positive alerts link to an incident record). LM-04 objectives test sample-of-evaluated-events-with-the, which no document proposes to source from this check. Alerts closed in bulk without an assignee, or auto resolved by automated investigation, are listed as such. Uses the NEW observation type endpoint.alert (id, device, severity, status, owner, created, updated, closed, classification).

checks.name: Protection blocks, not only detects
checks.description: Every active sensor runs under a policy that blocks or quarantines malware, with tamper or uninstall protection on.
checks.remediation: Move the listed sensors to a prevention policy and turn on tamper or uninstall protection.

controls.rationale: Shows agents are set to prevent. Coverage and alert handling are separate.

evidence_kinds: Per sensor: policy, prevention mode, tamper state

provider_notes.defender_endpoint: avMode active means blocking (the code table on Microsoft's page is ambiguous: verify). Tamper protection comes from Intune windowsProtectionState.tamperProtectionEnabled or the Intune DefenderAgents report, so it needs Intune data. Attack surface reduction and EDR block mode policies are not read (unverified). Passive mode does not block.
provider_notes.crowdstrike: The host's applied prevention policy has machine learning prevention and quarantine on (setting ids from fixtures), and its sensor update policy has uninstall protection on. Setting ids differ per platform and change over time: version the evaluation rule.
provider_notes.sentinelone: 5.5 says 'likely'. Effective policy mitigation mode protect and anti tamper on; policy inheritance (account, site, group) must be resolved per agent. Fields unverified.

checks.population: Active sensors in scope.
checks.predicate: The effective policy blocks or quarantines malware (not detect only) and tamper or uninstall protection is on.
checks.period: Daily snapshot.
checks.empty_population: Insufficient (shared rule 5.1).
checks.notes: Outcomes: fail when detect only, or tamper protection off; insufficient when the policy is not readable. No artifact is named in any document; the natural home is the proposed device-protection-agent-report (EP-01.B). Uses the NEW observation type endpoint.sensor (prevention mode, tamper protection, policy id).

checks.name: Every server runs the protection agent
checks.description: Every active server asset in production in the Verity asset register has a matching protection sensor, or an exemption with a reason reviewed in the last 12 months.
checks.remediation: Install the protection agent on the listed servers, or record an exemption with its reason and review it every year.

controls.rationale: Shows servers in the asset register are covered, and that exemptions are rechecked yearly.

evidence_kinds: Per asset: match key, sensor, exemption reason and date

provider_notes.defender_endpoint: Server assets matched by hostname or IP to machines. Cloud instances need the cloud resource id, which is not on the machine resource.
provider_notes.crowdstrike: Server assets matched by hostname, cloud instance id or MAC; product_type_desc Server.
provider_notes.sentinelone: Machine type server, matched by name or IP. Fields unverified.

checks.population: Active infrastructure and cloud assets with an operating system recorded, in production (setting), minus exemptions with a reason reviewed in the last 12 months.
checks.predicate: A matching sensor reported within the window.
checks.period: Daily snapshot; exemptions must have been reviewed within 12 months.
checks.empty_population: Insufficient (shared rule 5.1).
checks.notes: Outcomes: fail when no sensor, or an exemption older than 12 months; insufficient when the asset has no match keys. The asset side is Verity's own asset register, read from the module. crowdstrike-falcon.md and microsoft-defender-endpoint.md section 6 add it to asset-inventory for EP-01.B. Merger caution: asset-inventory is named by 27 objectives under combine any, so this check must fill it partially (rule A), otherwise a passing server coverage check could satisfy LM-01 inventory objectives. The proposed device-protection-agent-report is an alternative home. Uses the NEW observation type endpoint.sensor.

checks.name: Backups succeed
checks.description: Every failed backup in the last 30 days was followed by a good backup in time, and each database can be restored to a recent point.
checks.remediation: Fix the failing backup and confirm the next one completes.

controls.rationale: Shows backups ran and failures were followed by a good backup (BC-01.B, part of BC-01.C). The alert, ticket and cause are a person's record.

provider_notes.aws: AWS Backup ListBackupJobs (state, created after) for in scope resources, and RDS latest restorable time. Job history retention unverified.
provider_notes.azure: Recovery Services backup job history (endpoint not verified this round). SQL point in time restore is a platform feature, so SQL databases pass on retention alone.
provider_notes.gcp: Cloud SQL backup runs in the last 30 days (endpoint not verified this round).

parameters.follow_up_hours: default 48: a failed job must be followed by a completed job within this time
parameters.restorable_time_hours: 24: RDS latest restorable time must be this recent

checks.population: Backup jobs in the last 30 days for in scope resources (AWS Backup, Recovery Services, Cloud SQL backup runs); each RDS database's latest restorable time.
checks.predicate: Every failed, aborted or expired job was followed by a completed job for the same resource within the setting, and each RDS database's latest restorable time is within 24 hours.
checks.period: The last 30 days, evaluated daily.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable when AWS Backup is unused and no RDS exists (AWS); otherwise an unread scope is insufficient_information.
checks.notes: Not a duplicate of cloud.backups_enabled, which reads configuration (retention, PITR, plan coverage); this one reads operation. Fill: aws.md and azure.md add it with cloud.backups_enabled to backup-failure-alerts-and-follow-up (BC-01.B, BC-01.C), partial; gcp.md lists only cloud.backups_enabled on that artifact.

checks.name: Backups are kept apart
checks.description: Each vault that holds production backups is locked, or its backups are copied to another account or region.
checks.remediation: Lock the vault or copy backups to another account or region.

controls.rationale: The separate, immutable copy of BC-01.D. The review of restore rights is separate.

provider_notes.aws: backup:DescribeBackupVault (vault lock, minimum retention) and backup plan copy actions.
provider_notes.azure: Recovery Services vault immutability and soft delete settings; field names not verified this round.
provider_notes.gcp: Not in the first version: backup vault locks were not verified this round.

checks.population: Backup vaults holding production recovery points.
checks.predicate: Each vault is locked, or its plan copies to another account or Region.
checks.period: Read at each run; daily history.
checks.empty_population: Shared rule: not_applicable only when every production scope was read and holds no backup vault.
checks.notes: No artifact is named for this check in any of the six documents, so as proposed it changes no objective. BC-01.D is filled today through backup-policy-covering-scope-frequency-and and list-of-privileged-accounts-with-approval, neither of which is a vault settings export; the merger should pick or propose an artifact. Related azure.md and gcp.md need about Key Vault soft delete and purge protection protecting keys that protect backups (see decisions).

checks.name: Network traffic is logged
checks.description: Every production network that has at least one network interface keeps an active flow log.
checks.remediation: Turn on flow logs for the listed networks.

controls.rationale: Network traffic reaches a log store. Reviewing it is separate.

provider_notes.aws: ec2:DescribeFlowLogs: each VPC has an active flow log (any destination) for ALL or REJECT traffic.
provider_notes.azure: Network Watcher flow logs: each virtual network (or NSG) in a production subscription with at least one network interface has an enabled flow log.
provider_notes.gcp: Subnets in production projects have flow logs on; the field was not verified this round.

checks.population: VPCs (AWS), virtual networks or NSGs (Azure), subnets (Google Cloud) in production accounts, subscriptions or projects that hold at least one network interface.
checks.predicate: Each has an active flow log; on AWS for ALL or REJECT traffic, to any destination.
checks.period: Read at each run; daily history.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable only when every production scope was read and holds no network with an interface.
checks.notes: Not a duplicate of cloud.audit_logging (control plane activity). Fill conflict: aws.md adds it with cloud.audit_logging to evidence-logs-are-reviewed (LM-02.B, partial: sources reach a store, review is people's), while azure.md says evidence-logs-are-reviewed stays person and gcp.md does not list it. Depends on production marks per account, subscription or project.

checks.name: Cloud console users use two factor
checks.description: Every cloud user who can sign in to the console with a password has a second factor.
checks.remediation: Add a second factor for each listed user, or move them to single sign on and remove their password.

controls.rationale: The cloud console side of 'every user has a second factor'. The identity provider covers everyone who signs in through it.

provider_notes.aws: From the IAM credential report (iam:GenerateCredentialReport, iam:GetCredentialReport): password_enabled and mfa_active per user. Identity Center users only partly: their MFA settings are read where the API allows (unverified).
provider_notes.azure: Not applicable: people sign in through Entra ID; see entra-id.md (idp checks).
provider_notes.gcp: Not in the first version: people sign in through the identity provider (Workspace or Cloud Identity).

related.why: Local cloud users outside the identity provider; root is its own check.
Local cloud users outside the identity provider; root is its own check.

checks.population: IAM users with a console password in every in scope account; Identity Center users where the API shows MFA settings (unverified).
checks.predicate: Every IAM user with password_enabled TRUE has mfa_active TRUE.
checks.period: Read at each run; daily history. The credential report can be regenerated at most every 4 hours.
checks.empty_population: Shared AWS rule: not_applicable only when every account was read and no IAM user has a password; an unread account is insufficient_information.
checks.notes: Overlap review. Not a duplicate of cloud.root_account_mfa: that check covers only root and break glass accounts and also requires no root access keys (and accepts centralized root access management); this one covers every other IAM user with a console password. Not a duplicate of idp.mfa_enforced, which covers people signing in through the identity provider. Recommendation: keep as its own key rather than fold into cloud.root_account_mfa, because folding would change a shipped predicate and population. Fill: aws.md adds it with cloud.root_account_mfa to second-factor-enforcement-and-enrolled-users (IAM-03.B, IAM-03.C), partial, the AWS side only.

checks.name: A restore was tested this year
checks.description: Each type of production data store had at least one completed restore, or a restore testing plan run, in the last 12 months.
checks.remediation: Run a restore test, or set up a restore testing plan.

controls.rationale: A restore happened in the period (BC-02.B). Proving the data was complete (BC-02.C) and the times against targets (BC-02.D) stays with people.

provider_notes.aws: backup:ListRestoreJobs and backup:ListRestoreTestingPlans (operation name unverified). Not in the SecurityAudit managed policy, so the custom policy carries it.
provider_notes.azure: Not assessed: azure.md section 1 says restore tests stay with people.
provider_notes.gcp: Not assessed: gcp.md section 1 says restore tests are not proven.

checks.population: AWS Backup restore jobs and restore testing plans for production resources.
checks.predicate: At least one completed restore job, or a restore testing plan run, for each production data store type in the last 12 months.
checks.period: The last 12 months, evaluated weekly.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable when AWS Backup is unused; an unread account is insufficient_information.
checks.notes: Only aws.md defines it; azure.md and gcp.md do not list it in their reuse tables and say restore tests stay with people. Fill: restore-test-plan-and-results (BC-02.B; the artifact also serves BC-02.C and BC-02.E), partial.

checks.name: Stored secrets rotate
checks.description: Each secret in the cloud secrets manager has rotation on, or was changed within the set number of days.
checks.remediation: Turn on rotation, or rotate the listed secrets and record it.

controls.rationale: Rotation on schedule (NS-09.C). Secrets held outside the secrets manager are not seen.
Integration credentials kept as secrets rotate.

provider_notes.aws: secretsmanager:ListSecrets only (never returns values): rotation enabled, rotation rules, last rotated, last changed.
provider_notes.azure: Needs the custom Key Vault metadata reader role (data actions vaults/*/read and secrets/readMetadata/action). Predicate on Azure: each enabled secret has an expiry, or was updated within the setting. Vaults on the access policy model need an access policy.
provider_notes.gcp: Secret Manager secrets with a rotation schedule, or a version newer than the setting; fields not verified this round.

related.why: Different population, age limit and controls.
Different population, age limit and controls.

checks.population: Secrets in the cloud secrets manager (Secrets Manager, Key Vault secrets, Secret Manager) in production accounts, subscriptions or projects.
checks.predicate: Each secret has rotation enabled, or was last changed within the setting. Values are never read.
checks.period: Read at each run; daily history.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable when no secret exists and every production scope was read.
checks.notes: Overlap review. Not a duplicate of cloud.secrets_managed (a secrets manager is in use, NS-09) nor of cloud.machine_credentials_rotated (provider native keys younger than 90 days: IAM access keys, service account keys, storage account keys, Azure app credentials, IAM-10). Populations, thresholds (365 versus 90 days) and controls differ, so recommend keeping it as its own key rather than folding it into either. Meaning conflict: the Azure predicate accepts 'has an expiry', but an expiry date set on a secret does not show it is rotated; AWS and Google Cloud ask for rotation on or a recent change. Recommend aligning Azure to 'rotation policy or updated within the setting'. Fill: aws.md and azure.md add it with cloud.secrets_managed to secret-store-rotation-list (NS-09.B, NS-09.C, NS-09.D, SD-11.C); aws.md says full for Secrets Manager (names and dates, no values). gcp.md lists only cloud.secrets_managed there.

checks.name: Storage is not public
checks.description: Public access blocks are on for accounts and buckets, and no bucket, snapshot or image is shared with everyone.
checks.remediation: Turn on block public access for the account and remove public sharing from the listed buckets, snapshots and images.

controls.rationale: One of the hardening items the CIS benchmark sets: public storage is blocked. The rest of the baseline and its approved exceptions stay with cloud.hardening_baseline and people.
Shows the high risk regression 'public storage' is absent today. Alerting on it, and investigating each alert, are separate.

provider_notes.aws: Account level S3 block public access has all four flags on (or each bucket does); no bucket policy status is public; EBS snapshot and AMI block public access is on per Region; no EBS snapshot, AMI or RDS snapshot is shared with 'all'. Needs s3:GetAccountPublicAccessBlock, s3:GetBucketPublicAccessBlock, s3:GetBucketPolicyStatus, ec2:DescribeSnapshotAttribute, ec2:GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState, ec2:GetImageBlockPublicAccessState, ec2:DescribeImages, rds:DescribeDBSnapshotAttributes. A missing block configuration is a real finding, not an error.
provider_notes.azure: Every storage account has allowBlobPublicAccess false, or publicNetworkAccess Disabled. That the account flag blocks anonymous access for every container is Microsoft's documented behaviour, but the page was not re read this round (unverified).
provider_notes.gcp: Every bucket has publicAccessPrevention enforced (or inherits it from the organisation policy), and no resource has a binding to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers unless recorded as public by design. Bindings come from Security Reviewer (searchAllIamPolicies). The binding half reaches any resource type, not only storage.

checks.population: AWS: account level block public access per account, every S3 bucket, owned EBS snapshots and AMIs, and RDS snapshots, in every in scope account and enabled Region. Azure: every storage account in every in scope subscription. Google Cloud: every bucket and every IAM binding in every in scope project.
checks.predicate: Public access is blocked at account or bucket level and nothing is shared with everyone, using each cloud's fields in provider_notes. A resource recorded in Verity as public by design (with a reason) passes.
checks.period: Settings are read at each run; the daily result history is the Type 2 record.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable only when every account, subscription or project and every enabled Region was read and none holds storage of these types; any unread scope is insufficient_information.
checks.notes: No artifact names this check today. aws.md writes 'NEED cloud_infrastructure: a dated export of public storage settings' and says it would otherwise sit under alerts-on-drift-that-were-investigated; the artifact key here is an extractor placeholder (see artifacts_proposed). It maps only to NS-04 and LM-03, not to a data protection control; the merger may want to check whether a DM control fits better. The Google Cloud predicate also judges allUsers bindings on any resource, which is wider than storage. Related gcp.md need: preventive organisation level guardrails that block public storage (see decisions). Not a duplicate of any existing check.

checks.name: Threat findings are handled in time
checks.description: No threat finding at or above the set severity has stayed open longer than the response time.
checks.remediation: Investigate the listed findings and archive them with the outcome.

controls.rationale: No high finding sat unhandled past the response time (supports NS-05.C). The triage decision and its reason are a person's record.

provider_notes.aws: GuardDuty ListFindings and GetFindings, filtered to the severity setting and not archived. GuardDuty keeps findings about 90 days (unverified).
provider_notes.azure: Defender alerts with status Active older than the response time; alerts list path and api-version unverified this round.
provider_notes.gcp: Premium or Enterprise only: active Security Command Center findings of class threat at or above the severity setting; v2 finding field names to confirm in fixtures. On Standard the threat service is not available.

checks.population: Threat findings or alerts at or above the severity setting that are not archived or closed, from GuardDuty, Defender for Cloud or Security Command Center.
checks.predicate: None has stayed open longer than the response time setting.
checks.period: Read daily; findings open now, aged from first seen.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable when there are no findings (and the service is on and fully read); error when denied; insufficient_information when a scope was unread.
checks.notes: Not a duplicate of cloud.threat_detection (the service is on). azure.md section 5.3 leaves open whether this key widens to cover configuration rule findings with first seen and resolved times (NS-04, NS-05, NS-08, LM-03) or a new key is added; see decisions. Similar 'alerts handled in time' predicates may come from endpoint or alerting research; the merger should check for aliases there. Fill: sample-of-alerts-that-were-investigated (NS-05.C, NS-05.D, NS-05.E), partial, on all three clouds (Google Cloud on Premium or Enterprise only).

provider_notes.azure: Certificates in Key Vault (needs the Key Vault metadata reader role; certificate list path unverified): none expired, none expiring within 14 days without auto renewal.
